origin.name: OCLP's OpenCore config.plist, after hao-opencore (and golden-gate-live-text-service)
origin.note: in the image's EFI partition; dev images only (pack dev). Not declared here (plist.set has no data value yet): NVRAM.Add csr-active-config, which apply.sh ORs with 0x4 (task-for-pid)

edits.reason: hao-opencore's boot-args unchanged on dev images: hao_crash=1 left out: with it a dev image's first boot stalls before sandboxd (QEMU, ab855d51; without it the same image boots in 537 s); hao-runtime's fix is parked until after beta.1.

arg_reasons.keepsyms=1: OCLP's base config: a panic report keeps the kernel's symbols, so it names functions instead of bare addresses
arg_reasons.-lilubetaall: Lilu and its plug-ins (OCLP's graphics and hardware kexts) load although they do not list Darwin 27 as supported
arg_reasons.ipc_control_port_options=0: OCLP adds it whenever SIP is lowered (efi_builder/security.py): from macOS 12.3 Electron apps stop launching with SIP lowered unless the IPC control-port policy is relaxed
arg_reasons.amfi_get_out_of_my_way=1: hao-runtime signs each program's x86_64 slice ad hoc with that program's own entitlements, including Apple-private ones (launchd's); with AMFIPass alone AMFI rejects /sbin/launchd and the kernel panics
arg_reasons.amfi_force_policy=8: AMFI's dyld policy treats a restricted program (CS_RESTRICT: it holds entitlements) as restricted again although SIP's filesystem bit is allowed, as on a Mac with SIP on, so dyld denies it the DYLD_* path variables (DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES, library and framework paths) unless it also requires library validation, which keeps them as on a Mac with SIP on (owner D1, 2026-11-17). Not version-scoped: a Recovery booted through this OpenCore gets it too; the Recovery tools that insert libraries run in the NetBoot Recovery, whose config is OCLP's. Bit 0x8 of AMFI's force_policy (forceDefaultDyldEnvVarsPolicy) is read only by the dyld environment policy; nothing the image ships sets DYLD_* for an entitled program
arg_reasons.auxKCAtBoot=false: kernelmanagerd loads the System kernel collection at once instead of first building an auxiliary one: 27's kmutil cannot build an x86_64 collection, so that build failed at every boot and held the System collection (and with it the framebuffer and WindowServer) back about 18 s
